questions.stem: A 29-year-old woman reports increased vaginal discharge with a fishy odor that is most noticeable after intercourse, along with mild irritation. Speculum examination shows a thin, gray, homogeneous discharge adhering to the vaginal walls; the cervix appears normal. Vaginal pH is 5.2. Which of the following is most likely to be seen on saline wet mount of the discharge?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Budding yeast forms with pseudohyphae

choices.label: B
choices.text: Epithelial cells coated with adherent bacteria

choices.label: C
choices.text: Pear-shaped motile flagellated protozoa

choices.label: D
choices.text: Sheets of neutrophils among inflamed cells

choices.label: E
choices.text: Uniformly pale, translucent squamous cells only

explanation.summary: Clue cells (squamous epithelial cells coated with bacteria) are the characteristic microscopic finding of bacterial vaginosis.
explanation.whyCorrect: Thin gray homogeneous discharge, fishy odor worse after sex, a normal cervix, and pH above 4.5 point to bacterial vaginosis. Its characteristic wet-mount finding is the clue cell: a vaginal squamous epithelial cell with bacteria adhering to its surface, one of the four Amsel criteria.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Budding yeast with pseudohyphae indicate vaginal candidiasis, which has a thick 'cottage cheese' discharge, minimal odor, and a normal pH of 4.0-4.5.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Flagellated pyriform protozoa indicate trichomoniasis, which causes a frothy yellow-green discharge and may produce a strawberry cervix.
whyWrongByChoice.D: BV is a vaginosis, not a true 'itis': there is little inflammation and no white cells. Neutrophil-rich inflammation fits trichomoniasis.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Uniformly pale, translucent squamous cells are the normal appearance; this patient meets several Amsel criteria for BV, so clue cells are expected.

questions.stem: A 24-year-old woman has 4 days of intense vulvar itching and burning with urination. Examination shows erythema and edema of the vulva and vaginal mucosa with a thick, white, clumped discharge that has minimal odor. The cervix appears normal. Vaginal pH is 4.2. Which of the following is most likely to be seen on microscopy of the discharge?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Budding yeast with pseudohyphae

choices.label: B
choices.text: Lemon-shaped cells with four flagella

choices.label: C
choices.text: Pale squamous cells without organisms

choices.label: D
choices.text: Sheets of gram-variable coccobacilli

choices.label: E
choices.text: Squamous cells studded with coccobacilli

explanation.summary: Vulvovaginal candidiasis shows budding yeast and pseudohyphae on microscopy.
explanation.whyCorrect: Pruritus, vulvovaginal erythema and edema, a thick 'cottage cheese' discharge with little odor, a normal cervix, and a normal pH (4.0-4.5) are the classic picture of vaginal candidiasis. The classic microscopy finding is budding yeast with pseudohyphae.

whyWrongByChoice.B: Lemon-shaped flagellated protozoa indicate trichomoniasis, which raises pH above 4.5 and causes a frothy yellow-green malodorous discharge.
whyWrongByChoice.C: This patient is clearly symptomatic with inflammatory findings; microscopy is expected to show the causative yeast.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Gram-variable coccobacilli describe Gardnerella vaginalis of bacterial vaginosis, which does not produce marked erythema or a normal pH.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Clue cells (squamous cells coated with bacteria) indicate bacterial vaginosis, which has a pH above 4.5, a thin gray discharge, and a fishy odor.

questions.stem: A 22-year-old woman with several new sexual partners and inconsistent condom use has a frothy, yellow-green, malodorous vaginal discharge with vaginal soreness that worsens during intercourse. Vaginal pH is 6.0. Which of the following best describes the most likely causative organism?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Cyst-forming protozoan transmitted mainly by the fecal-oral route

choices.label: B
choices.text: Gram-negative diplococcus that infects the endocervical canal

choices.label: C
choices.text: Gram-variable coccobacillus that thrives as lactobacilli decline

choices.label: D
choices.text: Lemon-shaped protozoan with a single nucleus and four flagella

choices.label: E
choices.text: Opportunistic yeast that forms germ tubes when placed in serum

explanation.summary: Trichomonas vaginalis is a lemon-shaped, highly motile protozoan with a single nucleus, an undulating membrane, and four flagella at one end.
explanation.whyCorrect: A frothy yellow-green malodorous discharge, pH above 4.5, and high-risk sexual behavior indicate trichomoniasis. T. vaginalis is a protozoan that is lemon (pear) shaped, has a single nucleus and an undulating membrane, and is highly motile with four flagella at one end.

whyWrongByChoice.A: T. vaginalis lacks a cyst form, which is why it is transmitted essentially only through sexual contact.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Neisseria gonorrhoeae causes cervicitis and must be ruled out in vaginitis, but the frothy yellow-green discharge with high pH is the picture of trichomoniasis.
whyWrongByChoice.C: This describes Gardnerella vaginalis, the main organism of bacterial vaginosis, which causes a thin gray discharge with a fishy odor rather than a frothy yellow-green one.
whyWrongByChoice.E: This describes Candida, which produces a thick white discharge with minimal odor and a normal vaginal pH.

questions.stem: A 26-year-old woman is diagnosed with trichomoniasis by nucleic acid amplification testing. She has one male sexual partner, who has no symptoms. Which of the following is the most appropriate management?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Metronidazole vaginal gel for her; no treatment for her partner

choices.label: B
choices.text: Oral metronidazole for both of them and a pause in sexual activity

choices.label: C
choices.text: Oral metronidazole for her; treat her partner only if symptomatic

choices.label: D
choices.text: Single-dose oral fluconazole for both of them and condom use

choices.label: E
choices.text: Topical clotrimazole for her and condom use with her partner

explanation.summary: Trichomoniasis is treated with oral metronidazole, the partner is treated too, and sexual activity is paused until the infection clears.
explanation.whyCorrect: Metronidazole is the drug of choice for T. vaginalis, and the oral route is always preferred. Because the organism is sexually transmitted and colonizes the male urethra and prostate (usually without symptoms in men), the partner is also treated, and sex should be paused until the infection has cleared.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Topical metronidazole is ineffective for trichomoniasis because the organism lives in the urethra and perivaginal glands, and the partner must also be treated.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Male infection is typically asymptomatic, so waiting for symptoms would leave a reservoir for reinfection; the partner is treated regardless.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Fluconazole is an azole antifungal for candidiasis and has no role against a protozoan.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Clotrimazole is a topical antifungal for mild candidiasis and does not treat T. vaginalis.

questions.stem: A 31-year-old woman who douches daily and recently completed a course of antibiotics is diagnosed with bacterial vaginosis. Her vaginal pH is 5.4. Which of the following sequences best explains the rise in her vaginal pH?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Candida overgrowth consumes glycogen and depletes vaginal acid

choices.label: B
choices.text: Fewer lactobacilli make less lactic acid, and anaerobes flourish

choices.label: C
choices.text: Increased lactobacilli ferment sugars into alkaline by-products

choices.label: D
choices.text: Neutrophil influx releases alkaline granules into vaginal fluid

choices.label: E
choices.text: Trichomonad cytotoxins destroy epithelium and liberate base

explanation.summary: In BV, loss of lactobacilli reduces lactic acid, raising pH above 4.5, which in turn favors anaerobic overgrowth.
explanation.whyCorrect: Healthy vaginal lactobacilli metabolize sugars to lactic acid, keeping pH below 4.5 and protecting against anaerobes. Douching and antibiotics disrupt this microbiota; lactobacilli decline, lactic acid production falls, pH rises, and the higher pH promotes further anaerobic growth.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Candida does not deplete lactobacilli, and vaginal candidiasis keeps a normal pH of 4.0-4.5.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Lactobacilli produce lactic acid, which acidifies the vagina; BV is marked by a decrease in lactobacilli, not an increase.
whyWrongByChoice.D: BV has little inflammation and no white cells, so neutrophil products cannot explain the pH change.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Cytotoxic epithelial damage is the mechanism of trichomoniasis, not bacterial vaginosis.

questions.stem: A 17-year-old girl who has never been sexually active is diagnosed with bacterial vaginosis. Her mother, who accompanies her, is upset and asks whether the diagnosis means her daughter has been having sex. Which of the following is the most accurate response?

choices.label: A
choices.text: BV develops only after intercourse exposes the vagina to semen

choices.label: B
choices.text: BV follows ascending spread from an untreated cervicitis

choices.label: C
choices.text: BV is sexually transmitted, so she must have had a partner

choices.label: D
choices.text: BV reflects a flora imbalance and can occur without sex

choices.label: E
choices.text: BV results from yeast invading the vaginal epithelium

explanation.summary: Bacterial vaginosis is a flora imbalance, not an STI, and can develop in people who are abstinent.
explanation.whyCorrect: BV results from loss of microbial balance: lactobacilli decline and anaerobes overgrow. Sexual practices contribute to risk, but many other activities (douching, antibiotics, intravaginal products) can cause it, and abstinent people can develop BV. Of the three main causes of vaginitis, only trichomoniasis is a true STI.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Semen exposure can worsen odor and sex is a risk factor, but BV can develop without any sexual activity.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Untreated STIs can ascend and cause PID; BV is a vaginal flora disorder, not a consequence of cervicitis.
whyWrongByChoice.C: BV is not considered an STI; only trichomoniasis among the three main causes of vaginitis is.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Yeast invasion of tissue describes vaginal candidiasis, not bacterial vaginosis.

questions.stem: A 30-year-old woman with uncomplicated vulvovaginal candidiasis is treated with a single oral dose of fluconazole, and her symptoms resolve. Which of the following is the mechanism of action of this drug?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Blocks peptidoglycan cross-linking in the cell wall

choices.label: B
choices.text: Disables the undulating membrane that drives motility

choices.label: C
choices.text: Forms free radicals that fragment intracellular DNA

choices.label: D
choices.text: Inhibits ergosterol synthesis for the fungal cell membrane

choices.label: E
choices.text: Restores lactobacilli that ferment sugar into lactic acid

explanation.summary: Azole antifungals such as fluconazole act by inhibiting ergosterol synthesis.
explanation.whyCorrect: The main antifungal class used for vaginal candidiasis is the azoles, which inhibit ergosterol synthesis. A one-time oral dose of fluconazole is typically effective.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Peptidoglycan is a bacterial cell-wall component; it is not the azole target and is absent from fungi.
whyWrongByChoice.B: The undulating membrane belongs to T. vaginalis, a protozoan that is not treated with fluconazole.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Free-radical formation that destroys DNA is the mechanism of metronidazole, used for BV and trichomoniasis.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Azoles act directly on the fungus; candidiasis is not a lactobacillus-deficient state.

questions.stem: A 28-year-old woman was treated at an urgent care center with metronidazole vaginal gel for trichomoniasis. Three weeks later she still has a malodorous discharge and repeat testing remains positive for Trichomonas vaginalis. Her only partner completed oral therapy, and they have abstained since. Which of the following best explains her treatment failure?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Metronidazole has no activity against protozoal parasites

choices.label: B
choices.text: The gel raised vaginal pH above the drug's active range

choices.label: C
choices.text: The organism forms dormant cysts that resist metronidazole

choices.label: D
choices.text: The organism is a yeast that requires an azole antifungal

choices.label: E
choices.text: The organism persists in the urethra and perivaginal glands

explanation.summary: Topical metronidazole fails in trichomoniasis because T. vaginalis burrows into the urethra and perivaginal glands, where gel cannot reach therapeutic levels; oral therapy is always preferred.
explanation.whyCorrect: T. vaginalis does not just live on the surface of the vaginal canal; it burrows deep into the urethra and perivaginal glands, where topical gels cannot achieve drug levels needed for eradication. That is why the oral route of metronidazole is always preferred for trichomoniasis, unlike BV, where oral or vaginal gel may be used.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Metronidazole is effective against protozoal parasites and is the drug of choice for T. vaginalis; the problem is the route.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Nothing in the lecture attributes topical failure to pH; the explanation is that the gel cannot reach the organism's deeper sites.
whyWrongByChoice.C: T. vaginalis lacks a cyst form; this is why it depends on sexual transmission.
whyWrongByChoice.D: T. vaginalis is a flagellated protozoan, not a yeast.

questions.stem: A 36-year-old woman has vulvar pruritus and a thick white discharge. KOH preparation shows budding yeast with pseudohyphae, and vaginal pH is 4.3. Her friend recently had bacterial vaginosis with a pH of 5.5. Which of the following best explains why this patient's pH remains in the expected range?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Candida secretes lactic acid that re-acidifies the vagina

choices.label: B
choices.text: Candidiasis does not decrease the lactobacillus population

choices.label: C
choices.text: Fungal ergosterol buffers alkaline amines made by anaerobes

choices.label: D
choices.text: Neutrophils in candidiasis consume alkaline bacterial by-products

choices.label: E
choices.text: Yeast suppresses anaerobes by producing volatile amines itself

explanation.summary: Vaginal candidiasis is not associated with loss of lactobacilli, so pH stays 4.0-4.5, unlike BV and trichomoniasis (both above 4.5).
explanation.whyCorrect: Vaginal pH is set by lactobacilli converting sugars to lactic acid. In BV, lactobacilli decline and pH rises above 4.5; in trichomoniasis, inflammation secondarily reduces them. Vaginal candidiasis is not associated with a decrease in lactobacilli, so the pH remains in the expected 4.0-4.5 range, a key discriminating feature.

whyWrongByChoice.A: The acid comes from lactobacilli, not from Candida; the point is that lactobacilli are preserved.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Ergosterol is a fungal membrane sterol (the azole target), not a vaginal pH buffer.
whyWrongByChoice.D: The pH is normal because lactobacilli are intact, not because of any neutrophil effect on bacterial by-products.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Volatile amines come from anaerobic bacterial metabolism in BV; Candida infection has minimal or no odor.

questions.stem: A 27-year-old woman has symptoms suggestive of bacterial vaginosis. The clinician wants the laboratory test regarded as the reference standard, which is more specific for this diagnosis than bedside criteria, and the patient accepts waiting for the result. Which of the following tests should be ordered?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Gram stain of the vaginal discharge sample

choices.label: B
choices.text: KOH preparation to look for pseudohyphae

choices.label: C
choices.text: Saline wet mount scored by Amsel criteria

choices.label: D
choices.text: Vaginal pH measurement with indicator paper

choices.label: E
choices.text: Whiff test with 10% potassium hydroxide

explanation.summary: Gram stain is the reference-standard laboratory test for BV and is more specific than the Amsel criteria, but results are delayed.
explanation.whyCorrect: The Gram stain is the reference standard laboratory test for BV and is more specific than the Amsel criteria. Its drawback is that the sample is sent to a lab, so the diagnosis usually is not available during the office visit.

whyWrongByChoice.B: Pseudohyphae identify Candida and do not diagnose bacterial vaginosis.
whyWrongByChoice.C: The Amsel criteria can be applied in the office, but they rely on clinical diagnosis and leave more room for error than the Gram stain.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Vaginal pH above 4.5 is only one Amsel criterion and is also elevated in trichomoniasis.
whyWrongByChoice.E: A positive whiff test is only one of the four Amsel criteria and is not the reference standard.

questions.stem: A 23-year-old woman with a new sexual partner has a thin, grayish, malodorous vaginal discharge. Unlike typical cases of this discharge pattern, she also reports moderate to severe lower pelvic pain, and examination shows marked vulvovaginal swelling and erythema. Which of the following is the most appropriate next step?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Prescribe single-dose oral fluconazole for presumed yeast

choices.label: B
choices.text: Prescribe topical nystatin and reevaluate her in one month

choices.label: C
choices.text: Reassure her that most such cases resolve without treatment

choices.label: D
choices.text: Test for Neisseria gonorrhoeae and Chlamydia trachomatis

choices.label: E
choices.text: Treat for bacterial vaginosis with metronidazole and no other testing

explanation.summary: Moderate to severe pain or marked inflammation is not typical of BV and should raise suspicion for another infection, including STIs and PID.
explanation.whyCorrect: Pain with BV is usually mild; moderate to severe pain, swelling, or erythema should suggest an infection other than BV, and suspicion for pelvic inflammatory disease should increase. STIs such as N. gonorrhoeae and C. trachomatis cause similar symptoms, can coexist, and if untreated can cause PID, leading to infertility or chronic pain, so they must be ruled out.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Nothing suggests candidiasis (thick white discharge, normal pH); fluconazole would not address a possible STI.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Nystatin is a topical antifungal for mild candidiasis and would delay evaluation of a possible STI.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Self-resolution applies to many mild BV cases, not to a patient with severe pain and inflammation that raise concern for PID.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Treating for BV alone ignores findings that suggest a different or concurrent infection such as an STI with possible PID.

questions.stem: A 52-year-old woman with poorly controlled diabetes mellitus has had three episodes of vulvovaginal candidiasis this year. Which of the following best explains how her hyperglycemia predisposes her to these infections?

choices.label: A
choices.text: It depletes lactobacilli, raising pH so that anaerobes flourish

choices.label: B
choices.text: It impairs leukocyte function, blunting innate defense

choices.label: C
choices.text: It induces Candida to switch into a resistant cyst stage

choices.label: D
choices.text: It kills commensal bacteria, opening a niche for the yeast

choices.label: E
choices.text: It lowers vaginal pH below the range that suppresses yeast

explanation.summary: Hyperglycemia impairs leukocyte function, inhibiting the innate response to Candida.
explanation.whyCorrect: Poorly controlled diabetes, immunosuppression, and antibiotic use increase the likelihood of vaginal candidiasis. Hyperglycemia specifically affects leukocyte function, inhibiting the innate immune response to Candida so colonizing yeast can invade tissue.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Lactobacillus depletion with anaerobic overgrowth is the mechanism of bacterial vaginosis, not candidiasis.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Candida forms yeasts and pseudohyphae, not cysts.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Killing commensal flora to open a niche is how antibiotics predispose to candidiasis, not how hyperglycemia does.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Vaginal candidiasis occurs with a normal pH of 4.0-4.5; the lecture does not describe hyperglycemia acting through pH.

questions.stem: A 23-year-old man has had 2 days of painful urination and a copious, frankly purulent penile discharge that began abruptly. There are no lesions on the external genitalia. Which of the following organisms is the most likely cause?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Chlamydia trachomatis

choices.label: B
choices.text: Escherichia coli

choices.label: C
choices.text: Herpes simplex virus

choices.label: D
choices.text: Neisseria gonorrhoeae

choices.label: E
choices.text: Staphylococcus saprophyticus

explanation.summary: An acute, frankly purulent urethral discharge suggests gonorrhea rather than chlamydia.
explanation.whyCorrect: N. gonorrhoeae and C. trachomatis are the two most important causes of urethritis and are often clinically indistinguishable. Gonorrhea, however, tends to be more acute, and a frankly purulent penile discharge points toward N. gonorrhoeae.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Chlamydia is more often subacute or unnoticed; dysuria alone with little discharge is more typical of C. trachomatis.
whyWrongByChoice.B: E. coli is a leading cause of cystitis, which typically does not produce urethral discharge.
whyWrongByChoice.C: HSV is suggested by external genital ulcers, fever, and tender inguinal lymphadenopathy, none of which are present.
whyWrongByChoice.E: S. saprophyticus causes urinary tract infections, not purulent STI urethritis.

questions.topicName: Urethritis, Cervicitis, and Pelvic Inflammatory Disease

questions.stem: A 20-year-old woman has mucopurulent cervical discharge and mild dysuria. Her clinician wants the single most accurate test to identify the causative pathogen. Which of the following is the gold standard?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Bacterial culture of a cervical swab

choices.label: B
choices.text: Diagnostic laparoscopy

choices.label: C
choices.text: Gram stain of cervical exudate

choices.label: D
choices.text: Nucleic acid amplification testing

choices.label: E
choices.text: Transvaginal ultrasonography

explanation.summary: NAAT is the gold standard diagnostic test for urethritis and cervicitis.
explanation.whyCorrect: NAAT is rapid and highly sensitive and can detect C. trachomatis, N. gonorrhoeae, M. genitalium, HSV, and other agents from a swab or urine specimen. It is the gold standard for diagnosing urethritis and cervicitis.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Culture is time consuming; its main value is determining antibiotic susceptibility.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Laparoscopy is the best test for uncertain PID, not for diagnosing cervicitis.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Gram stain is seldom used because C. trachomatis and viruses cannot be seen and the sample may be insufficient.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Transvaginal ultrasonography images pelvic structures and cannot identify an organism in cervicitis.

questions.topicName: Urethritis, Cervicitis, and Pelvic Inflammatory Disease

questions.stem: A 26-year-old man has dysuria, fever, and headache. Examination shows several painful shallow ulcers on the penile shaft and tender bilateral inguinal lymphadenopathy. Which of the following is the most likely cause?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Chlamydia trachomatis

choices.label: B
choices.text: Herpes simplex virus

choices.label: C
choices.text: Mycoplasma genitalium

choices.label: D
choices.text: Neisseria gonorrhoeae

choices.label: E
choices.text: Trichomonas vaginalis

explanation.summary: Genital ulcers with fever, headache, and tender inguinal nodes point to HSV rather than gonorrhea or chlamydia.
explanation.whyCorrect: When urethritis is accompanied by genital ulceration or other external lesions, a cause other than N. gonorrhoeae or C. trachomatis should be sought. External genital ulcers are strongly associated with HSV, which also causes fever, tender local inguinal lymphadenopathy, and headache.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Chlamydia causes subacute urethritis and does not produce the ulcers seen here.
whyWrongByChoice.C: M. genitalium is an increasingly recognized cause of urethritis but not of ulcerative lesions.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Gonorrhea causes urethritis with purulent discharge but does not explain genital ulcers.
whyWrongByChoice.E: T. vaginalis can cause urethritis but is not associated with genital ulcers and tender adenopathy.

questions.topicName: Urethritis, Cervicitis, and Pelvic Inflammatory Disease

questions.stem: A 25-year-old woman has had worsening lower abdominal pain for 2 days and a temperature of 38.4°C. During bimanual examination, she cries out and lifts her hips off the table when the clinician gently moves the cervix. Which of the following conditions does this finding most strongly suggest?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Acute bacterial cystitis

choices.label: B
choices.text: Acute pyelonephritis

choices.label: C
choices.text: Isolated gonococcal urethritis

choices.label: D
choices.text: Pelvic inflammatory disease

choices.label: E
choices.text: Vaginal cellulitis

explanation.summary: Cervical motion tenderness (the chandelier sign) indicates PID.
explanation.whyCorrect: Bimanual findings that indicate PID are lower abdominal tenderness, adnexal tenderness, and cervical motion tenderness. The last is called the chandelier sign because manipulation of the cervix is so painful the patient seems to leap toward the chandelier.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Cystitis is a lower urinary tract infection and does not produce cervical motion tenderness.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Pyelonephritis is an upper urinary tract infection of the kidney and does not cause cervical motion tenderness.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Isolated urethritis presents with dysuria and discharge, not fever and severe pain on cervical movement.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Vaginal cellulitis is a localized soft tissue infection of the vaginal wall, not an upper tract inflammation.

questions.topicName: Urethritis, Cervicitis, and Pelvic Inflammatory Disease

questions.stem: Ascending gonococcal and chlamydial infections in females can progress to peritonitis and sepsis, whereas upper reproductive tract infections in males generally cause less severe systemic illness. Which of the following anatomic features best explains this difference?

choices.label: A
choices.text: The cervix normally provides no barrier to vaginal organisms

choices.label: B
choices.text: The endometrium is normally colonized by vaginal organisms

choices.label: C
choices.text: The fallopian tubes open directly into the peritoneal cavity

choices.label: D
choices.text: The ovaries form a closed system with the fallopian tubes

choices.label: E
choices.text: The shorter female urethra lets organisms reach the bladder

explanation.summary: The open fimbriated ends of the fallopian tubes let pathogens spill into the peritoneum.
explanation.whyCorrect: The fallopian tubes open into the peritoneal cavity and do not form a closed system with the ovaries. Bacteria can therefore spill into the peritoneum and reach the blood, causing peritonitis and sepsis. The male tract has no such opening, so men generally do not become as sick.

whyWrongByChoice.A: The cervix normally functions as a barrier protecting the sterile upper tract.
whyWrongByChoice.B: The upper reproductive tract, including the uterus, is normally sterile.
whyWrongByChoice.D: The tubes and ovaries do not form a closed system; that openness is the problem.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Urethral length relates to bladder infection, not to spread of infection into the peritoneum.

questions.topicName: Urethritis, Cervicitis, and Pelvic Inflammatory Disease

questions.stem: A 24-year-old woman is diagnosed with pelvic inflammatory disease. Her cervical NAAT is pending. The clinician prescribes ceftriaxone and doxycycline and also adds metronidazole. Which of the following is the primary reason for adding metronidazole?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Coverage of anaerobic vaginal flora

choices.label: B
choices.text: Coverage of Candida species

choices.label: C
choices.text: Coverage of herpes simplex virus

choices.label: D
choices.text: Coverage of Mycoplasma genitalium

choices.label: E
choices.text: Coverage of Staphylococcus saprophyticus

explanation.summary: PID is polymicrobial, so therapy must cover gonorrhea, chlamydia, and anaerobic vaginal flora.
explanation.whyCorrect: Although PID usually begins with N. gonorrhoeae or C. trachomatis, a compromised cervix lets opportunistic vaginal and gastrointestinal organisms (e.g., Prevotella, Leptotrichia, Atopobium) ascend. Treatment must therefore also cover anaerobic vaginal flora, which is the role of metronidazole.

whyWrongByChoice.B: Candida is a fungus and is not the reason metronidazole is included.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Metronidazole has no antiviral activity; HSV is not the target of the PID regimen.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Metronidazole is not added to target M. genitalium in the PID regimen.
whyWrongByChoice.E: S. saprophyticus is a urinary tract pathogen, not part of the PID coverage rationale.

questions.topicName: Urethritis, Cervicitis, and Pelvic Inflammatory Disease

questions.stem: A 29-year-old woman has an atypical 5-day history of vague pelvic pain and low-grade fever. Bimanual examination findings are equivocal, transvaginal ultrasonography is nondiagnostic, and several other causes of abdominopelvic pain remain under consideration. Which of the following is the best test to establish whether she has pelvic inflammatory disease?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Blood cultures from two sites

choices.label: B
choices.text: Complete blood count with differential

choices.label: C
choices.text: Diagnostic laparoscopy

choices.label: D
choices.text: Gram stain of cervical exudate

choices.label: E
choices.text: Repeat transvaginal ultrasonography

explanation.summary: Diagnostic laparoscopy is the best test for PID, reserved for uncertain or atypical cases.
explanation.whyCorrect: PID is usually a clinical diagnosis. Diagnostic laparoscopy is the best test because it directly identifies inflammation and infection, but because it is invasive it is reserved for uncertain diagnoses or atypical presentations such as this one.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Blood cultures are often negative in PID and cannot establish the diagnosis.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Leukocytosis is common but nonspecific and cannot confirm PID.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Gram stain cannot visualize C. trachomatis and does not confirm upper tract inflammation.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Transvaginal ultrasonography has poor sensitivity and specificity for PID; repeating it adds little.

questions.topicName: Urethritis, Cervicitis, and Pelvic Inflammatory Disease

questions.stem: A 27-year-old woman recently treated for pelvic inflammatory disease develops right upper quadrant pain that worsens with deep breathing and coughing. Liver enzymes are normal. Laparoscopy shows thin fibrous bands stretching from the surface of the liver to the anterior abdominal wall. Which of the following structures is primarily inflamed?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Common bile duct epithelium

choices.label: B
choices.text: Gallbladder mucosa

choices.label: C
choices.text: Glisson capsule

choices.label: D
choices.text: Hepatocellular parenchyma

choices.label: E
choices.text: Right diaphragmatic muscle

explanation.summary: Fitz-Hugh-Curtis syndrome is perihepatitis of the Glisson capsule, not the liver parenchyma.
explanation.whyCorrect: About 10% of PID cases result in perihepatitis (Fitz-Hugh-Curtis syndrome), an inflammation of the Glisson capsule surrounding the liver. It causes RUQ pain worsened by breathing, coughing, or movement and produces thin violin-string adhesions between the liver capsule and the anterior abdominal wall or diaphragm.

whyWrongByChoice.A: The biliary tree is not the site of inflammation in this PID complication.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Gallbladder inflammation does not produce violin-string adhesions from the liver surface after PID.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Fitz-Hugh-Curtis spares the parenchyma; it is a capsular inflammation.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Adhesions may reach the diaphragm, but the inflamed structure is the liver capsule.

questions.topicName: Urethritis, Cervicitis, and Pelvic Inflammatory Disease

questions.stem: A 22-year-old woman with cervicitis has a cervical culture that grows Neisseria gonorrhoeae. No testing for Chlamydia trachomatis was sent, and she is not pregnant. Which of the following is the most appropriate treatment?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Azithromycin 1000 mg orally as one dose alone

choices.label: B
choices.text: Ceftriaxone IM once plus doxycycline for 7 days

choices.label: C
choices.text: Ceftriaxone IM once plus metronidazole for 14 days

choices.label: D
choices.text: Ceftriaxone IM once with no additional agent

choices.label: E
choices.text: Doxycycline for 7 days with no ceftriaxone

explanation.summary: Gonococcal cervicitis is treated with single-dose IM ceftriaxone, adding 7 days of doxycycline when chlamydia has not been excluded.
explanation.whyCorrect: The recommended treatment for gonococcal urethritis or cervicitis is a single intramuscular dose of ceftriaxone. Because chlamydial infection has not been excluded in this patient, doxycycline for 7 days is added.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Single-dose azithromycin is the adherence alternative for nongonococcal infection, not gonorrhea therapy.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Metronidazole for 14 days is part of the PID regimen, not the treatment of uncomplicated cervicitis.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Ceftriaxone alone is appropriate only once chlamydia has been excluded.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Doxycycline alone is for nongonococcal infection and does not treat her confirmed gonorrhea.

questions.topicName: Urethritis, Cervicitis, and Pelvic Inflammatory Disease

questions.stem: A 26-year-old woman at 14 weeks' gestation has mucopurulent cervical discharge. NAAT is positive for both Neisseria gonorrhoeae and Chlamydia trachomatis. Which of the following is the most appropriate treatment?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Azithromycin as a single dose alone

choices.label: B
choices.text: Ceftriaxone IM plus azithromycin as a single dose

choices.label: C
choices.text: Ceftriaxone IM plus doxycycline for 7 days

choices.label: D
choices.text: Ceftriaxone IM plus metronidazole for 14 days

choices.label: E
choices.text: Doxycycline for 7 days as sole therapy

explanation.summary: In pregnancy, gonorrhea is still treated with ceftriaxone, but chlamydia is treated with single-dose azithromycin instead of doxycycline.
explanation.whyCorrect: Ceftriaxone remains the recommended treatment for gonorrhea during pregnancy. When chlamydial treatment is also needed in pregnancy, azithromycin as a single dose is used rather than doxycycline.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Azithromycin alone treats the chlamydia but leaves the gonorrhea without ceftriaxone.
whyWrongByChoice.C: This is the nonpregnant regimen; doxycycline is avoided for chlamydia in pregnancy.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Metronidazole covers anaerobes in PID and does not treat chlamydia.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Doxycycline is avoided in pregnancy and does not treat her gonorrhea.

questions.topicName: Urethritis, Cervicitis, and Pelvic Inflammatory Disease

questions.stem: A 21-year-old nonpregnant woman is diagnosed with mild-to-moderate pelvic inflammatory disease. She is tolerating oral intake, appears well, and has no adnexal mass on ultrasonography. Which of the following is the most appropriate outpatient regimen?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Azithromycin 1000 mg once plus metronidazole for 7 days

choices.label: B
choices.text: Ceftriaxone IM once plus azithromycin 1000 mg once

choices.label: C
choices.text: Ceftriaxone IM once plus doxycycline alone for 7 days

choices.label: D
choices.text: Ceftriaxone IM once plus doxycycline and metronidazole for 14 days

choices.label: E
choices.text: Doxycycline and metronidazole for 7 days without ceftriaxone

explanation.summary: Outpatient PID therapy is ceftriaxone IM once plus 14 days of doxycycline and metronidazole.
explanation.whyCorrect: PID is polymicrobial, so therapy must cover N. gonorrhoeae, C. trachomatis, and anaerobic vaginal flora. Mild-to-moderate PID can usually be treated as an outpatient with ceftriaxone IM once plus doxycycline and metronidazole, both for 14 days.

whyWrongByChoice.A: This omits gonococcal coverage and is too short.
whyWrongByChoice.B: This lacks anaerobic coverage and the 14-day course required for PID.
whyWrongByChoice.C: This is the gonococcal cervicitis regimen; it lacks anaerobic coverage and is too short for PID.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Omitting ceftriaxone leaves gonorrhea uncovered, and 7 days is too short for PID.

questions.topicName: Urethritis, Cervicitis, and Pelvic Inflammatory Disease

questions.stem: A 24-year-old nonpregnant woman began outpatient therapy for pelvic inflammatory disease 3 days ago. She has taken every dose, yet her fever and pelvic pain are unchanged. Transvaginal ultrasonography shows no adnexal fluid collection. Which of the following is the most appropriate next step?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Admit to the hospital for parenteral antibiotic therapy

choices.label: B
choices.text: Continue the same oral regimen for the full 14 days

choices.label: C
choices.text: Schedule elective adnexectomy on an outpatient basis

choices.label: D
choices.text: Stop antibiotics and repeat cervical NAAT in 1 week

choices.label: E
choices.text: Switch to single-dose oral azithromycin monotherapy

explanation.summary: Failure to improve within 72 hours of outpatient PID therapy is an indication for hospitalization and parenteral therapy.
explanation.whyCorrect: Hospitalization and parenteral therapy are appropriate for patients who are pregnant, have a tubo-ovarian abscess or severe illness, cannot tolerate outpatient therapy, fail to improve within 72 hours, or need evaluation for a surgical emergency. After clinical improvement, oral doxycycline and metronidazole complete 14 days.

whyWrongByChoice.B: Continuing an unsuccessful outpatient regimen ignores failure to improve within 72 hours.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Adnexectomy is reserved for severe tubo-ovarian abscess, which she does not have.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Stopping treatment risks long-term complications such as infertility and abscess.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Azithromycin monotherapy lacks gonococcal and anaerobic coverage for PID.

questions.topicName: Urethritis, Cervicitis, and Pelvic Inflammatory Disease

questions.stem: A 27-year-old man comes to the emergency department 2 hours after abrupt onset of severe left scrotal pain that woke him from sleep. He is afebrile and has no dysuria or urethral discharge. The left testis is exquisitely tender, and stroking the inner thigh produces no retraction of the left testis. Color Doppler ultrasonography shows diminished flow to the left testis. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Acute bacterial epididymitis

choices.label: B
choices.text: Autoimmune orchitis

choices.label: C
choices.text: Epididymo-orchitis

choices.label: D
choices.text: Mumps orchitis

choices.label: E
choices.text: Testicular torsion

explanation.summary: Sudden severe pain, no fever, an absent cremasteric reflex and reduced blood flow point to torsion, the most time-sensitive cause of acute scrotal pain.
explanation.whyCorrect: Torsion is of sudden onset with severe pain, reduced testicular blood flow and typically no fever, and the cremasteric reflex is frequently absent. It is the first diagnosis to exclude in acute scrotal pain because it must be identified quickly and treated surgically.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Epididymitis develops gradually, often with dysuria or discharge, has an intact cremasteric reflex and shows hyperemia on Doppler.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Autoimmune orchitis is a rare noninfectious inflammation causing impaired spermatogenesis, not an abrupt vascular emergency with lost flow.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Epididymo-orchitis is inflammatory, with increased blood flow and an intact cremasteric reflex.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Mumps orchitis is of gradual onset, often follows parotitis, keeps the cremasteric reflex intact and shows increased (not reduced) blood flow.

questions.stem: A 19-year-old college student has had painful swelling of both cheeks just in front of the ears for 5 days. He now reports progressive right testicular pain. He has no record of childhood immunizations. He is sexually inactive. Examination shows diffuse swelling and exquisite tenderness of the right testis; the cremasteric reflex is intact. Urinalysis is normal. Which of the following is the most likely cause of his testicular findings?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Chlamydia trachomatis

choices.label: B
choices.text: Coxsackie B virus

choices.label: C
choices.text: Escherichia coli

choices.label: D
choices.text: Mumps orthorubulavirus

choices.label: E
choices.text: Neisseria gonorrhoeae

explanation.summary: Isolated orchitis in an unvaccinated postpubertal male after parotitis is mumps orchitis.
explanation.whyCorrect: Isolated orchitis is primarily viral and specifically due to mumps; lack of MMR vaccination is the dominant risk factor. Orchitis typically follows parotitis by 4-6 days, is most likely after puberty, and leaves urinalysis normal because spread is hematogenous.

whyWrongByChoice.A: C. trachomatis causes STI-associated epididymo-orchitis with urethritis and pyuria, not orchitis after parotitis in a sexually inactive man.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Coxsackie B is a rare cause of viral orchitis and is not associated with preceding parotitis.
whyWrongByChoice.C: E. coli causes epididymitis tied to urinary infection or urologic disease, with abnormal urinalysis.
whyWrongByChoice.E: N. gonorrhoeae causes epididymo-orchitis via urethritis; urinalysis would typically show pyuria.

questions.stem: A 23-year-old man has had dysuria and a thin urethral discharge for 10 days. Over the past 3 days he has developed gradually worsening pain behind the left testis. He has had several new sexual partners this year. Temperature is 37.9 C. There is focal tenderness over the posterior epididymis and a thickened spermatic cord; the cremasteric reflex is present. Which of the following organisms is the most likely cause?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Chlamydia trachomatis

choices.label: B
choices.text: Escherichia coli

choices.label: C
choices.text: Mumps orthorubulavirus

choices.label: D
choices.text: Mycobacterium tuberculosis

choices.label: E
choices.text: Pseudomonas aeruginosa

explanation.summary: Epididymitis in men under 35 is usually an STI complication, most often C. trachomatis or N. gonorrhoeae.
explanation.whyCorrect: Epididymitis in adolescents and younger men is usually due to STI, most often C. trachomatis and N. gonorrhoeae, spreading from urethritis to the epididymis. Urethral discharge and dysuria preceding gradual posterior testicular pain fit this ascending pattern.

whyWrongByChoice.B: E. coli is the typical cause in boys with UTI and in older men with urologic disease, not a young man with urethritis and new partners.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Mumps causes orchitis after parotitis via hematogenous spread, not urethral discharge with epididymal tenderness.
whyWrongByChoice.D: M. tuberculosis is an uncommon cause, seen especially in HIV-positive patients.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Pseudomonas is a cause in older men, particularly with urinary stasis or instrumentation.

questions.stem: A 71-year-old man with benign prostatic hypertrophy had an indwelling urethral catheter placed during a hospitalization 1 week ago. He now has 3 days of gradually worsening right scrotal pain and a temperature of 38.4 C. He has been in a monogamous marriage for 45 years. The right scrotum is warm, erythematous and tender posteriorly. Urinalysis shows pyuria. Which of the following is the most likely causative organism?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Chlamydia trachomatis

choices.label: B
choices.text: Escherichia coli

choices.label: C
choices.text: Mumps orthorubulavirus

choices.label: D
choices.text: Neisseria gonorrhoeae

choices.label: E
choices.text: Treponema pallidum

explanation.summary: In men 35 and older, epididymitis usually stems from urologic conditions and is caused by coliforms such as E. coli.
explanation.whyCorrect: In older men, epididymitis is commonly due to BPH with urinary stasis, urinary tract infection or catheterization, and the organisms are E. coli, other gram-negative bacteria and gram-positive cocci. His catheter, BPH and low STI risk all point to a urinary pathogen.

whyWrongByChoice.A: C. trachomatis predominates in sexually active men under 35; this man has low STI risk and an instrumentation history.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Mumps is a cause of orchitis in unvaccinated postpubertal males, not catheter-associated epididymitis with pyuria.
whyWrongByChoice.D: N. gonorrhoeae is an STI cause typical of younger men, not a catheterized older man in a long monogamous marriage.
whyWrongByChoice.E: T. pallidum is a less common cause of epididymitis seen as part of syphilis.

questions.stem: A 26-year-old man has 4 days of dysuria, purulent urethral discharge and gradually increasing pain over the posterior aspect of the left testis. The cremasteric reflex is intact and Doppler shows increased epididymal flow. A first-void urine NAAT is sent. Which of the following is the most appropriate empiric management while results are pending?

choices.label: A
choices.text: IM ceftriaxone as a single agent

choices.label: B
choices.text: IM ceftriaxone plus oral doxycycline

choices.label: C
choices.text: NSAIDs, ice and scrotal elevation only

choices.label: D
choices.text: Oral levofloxacin alone

choices.label: E
choices.text: Oral trimethoprim-sulfamethoxazole alone

explanation.summary: Suspected STI-related epididymitis is treated with ceftriaxone (gonorrhea) plus doxycycline (chlamydia).
explanation.whyCorrect: When an STI is suspected, oral doxycycline and IM or IV ceftriaxone should be given. Ceftriaxone covers N. gonorrhoeae and doxycycline covers C. trachomatis, the two most common causes in men under 35; NSAIDs and scrotal support can be added for symptoms.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Ceftriaxone alone covers N. gonorrhoeae but leaves C. trachomatis untreated.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Supportive care alone is appropriate for mumps orchitis, not bacterial epididymitis.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Levofloxacin is chosen for men 35 and older at low STI risk to cover urinary pathogens.
whyWrongByChoice.E: TMP-SMX targets urinary-associated bacteria in low-STI-risk older men, not gonorrhea and chlamydia.

questions.stem: A 64-year-old man with benign prostatic hypertrophy and urinary hesitancy has 4 days of gradually worsening left scrotal pain. He has had one sexual partner, his wife, for 38 years. The left epididymis is swollen and tender; the cremasteric reflex is intact. Urinalysis shows leukocyte esterase and pyuria. NAAT for C. trachomatis and N. gonorrhoeae is negative. Which of the following is the most appropriate antibiotic therapy?

choices.label: A
choices.text: IM ceftriaxone alone

choices.label: B
choices.text: IM ceftriaxone plus oral doxycycline

choices.label: C
choices.text: No antibiotics; supportive care only

choices.label: D
choices.text: Oral doxycycline alone

choices.label: E
choices.text: Oral levofloxacin

explanation.summary: Men 35 and older at low STI risk receive levofloxacin or TMP-SMX to cover urinary pathogens.
explanation.whyCorrect: For men aged 35 and older at low risk for STIs, typical treatment is oral levofloxacin or trimethoprim-sulfamethoxazole, both of which cover urinary-associated bacteria such as E. coli. His BPH, pyuria and negative NAAT fit a urinary source.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Ceftriaxone is included to cover N. gonorrhoeae in STI-related disease.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Ceftriaxone plus doxycycline targets gonorrhea and chlamydia, the regimen for suspected STI.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Supportive care alone is for viral (mumps) orchitis; bacterial epididymitis requires antibiotics.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Doxycycline alone covers chlamydia, which is unlikely here, and is not the urinary-pathogen choice.

questions.stem: A 17-year-old unvaccinated boy developed parotid swelling 6 days ago and now has painful swelling of the left testis. RT-PCR of a buccal swab confirms mumps. Urinalysis is normal and Doppler shows testicular hyperemia. Which of the following is the most appropriate management?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Emergent scrotal surgical exploration

choices.label: B
choices.text: IM ceftriaxone plus oral doxycycline

choices.label: C
choices.text: NSAIDs, ice, scrotal elevation and rest

choices.label: D
choices.text: Oral levofloxacin for urinary pathogens

choices.label: E
choices.text: Oral trimethoprim-sulfamethoxazole course

explanation.summary: Mumps orchitis is viral, so treatment is supportive rather than antibiotic-based.
explanation.whyCorrect: When mumps is the cause, treatment is supportive: analgesics (NSAIDs), ice, scrotal elevation and rest. Antibiotics do not treat a viral infection; prevention depends on MMR vaccination.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Surgical exploration is for torsion; hyperemia on Doppler and confirmed mumps argue against it.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Ceftriaxone plus doxycycline covers gonorrhea and chlamydia and has no role in viral orchitis.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Levofloxacin covers urinary bacteria in older low-STI-risk men and does not treat mumps.
whyWrongByChoice.E: TMP-SMX is an alternative for bacterial epididymitis from urinary pathogens, not viral orchitis.

questions.stem: A 30-year-old man has 3 days of gradually worsening right scrotal pain with dysuria. The right hemiscrotum is warm and erythematous. Which of the following examination findings would best support epididymitis over testicular torsion?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Diffuse scrotal tenderness on palpation

choices.label: B
choices.text: Mild erythema of the scrotal skin

choices.label: C
choices.text: Pain relief when the testis is lifted

choices.label: D
choices.text: Testis retracts when the inner thigh is stroked

choices.label: E
choices.text: Tightness of the scrotum with a drawn-up testis

explanation.summary: An intact cremasteric reflex supports epididymitis; the reflex is frequently absent in torsion.
explanation.whyCorrect: The cremasteric reflex, retraction of the testis on stroking the inner thigh, is intact in epididymitis, orchitis and epididymo-orchitis but frequently absent in torsion, so examining it helps distinguish them.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Tenderness is present in both inflammatory conditions and torsion and does not separate them.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Scrotal erythema can accompany several causes of scrotal pain and is not discriminating.
whyWrongByChoice.C: A positive Prehn sign may occur in epididymitis but is not specific and is seen in other testicular disorders.
whyWrongByChoice.E: A tight scrotum with a drawn-up testis can be seen in epididymitis and does not reliably exclude torsion.

questions.stem: A 22-year-old man presents with gradual-onset posterior testicular pain, dysuria and scant urethral discharge. The physician wants the most accurate test for C. trachomatis and N. gonorrhoeae. Which of the following specimens and methods is most appropriate?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Blood culture drawn before antibiotics

choices.label: B
choices.text: Culture of a midstream urine specimen

choices.label: C
choices.text: NAAT of a first-void urine specimen

choices.label: D
choices.text: NAAT of a urethral swab specimen

choices.label: E
choices.text: RT-PCR of a saliva specimen

explanation.summary: NAAT on first-void urine is the more accurate specimen for chlamydia and gonorrhea.
explanation.whyCorrect: NAAT can be performed on first-void urine or a urethral swab, and first-void urine is the more accurate specimen. It detects C. trachomatis and N. gonorrhoeae and is helpful in symptomatic men under 35 or at STI risk.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Blood cultures are indicated only if the patient has a fever and do not detect chlamydia.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Routine urine culture is positive in only about a quarter of epididymitis cases and does not detect chlamydia.
whyWrongByChoice.D: A urethral swab NAAT is acceptable but less accurate than first-void urine.
whyWrongByChoice.E: RT-PCR of saliva or buccal swab is used to diagnose mumps, not STIs.

questions.stem: A 20-year-old man with confirmed mumps has painful swelling of the right testis. Urinalysis shows no leukocytes, negative leukocyte esterase and no bacteria. Which of the following best explains the urinalysis findings?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Infection ascends via the vas deferens, bypassing the bladder

choices.label: B
choices.text: Mumps virus suppresses neutrophil entry into the urine

choices.label: C
choices.text: Orchitis precedes urethral involvement by several weeks

choices.label: D
choices.text: Parotid inflammation sequesters circulating leukocytes

choices.label: E
choices.text: Viral spread is hematogenous rather than ascending

explanation.summary: Mumps orchitis follows hematogenous spread, so there is no urethritis, pyuria or bacteriuria.
explanation.whyCorrect: Mumps-related orchitis results from hematogenous spread of the virus, not ascending infection. Because the urinary tract is not involved, there is typically no urethritis, no pyuria and no bacteriuria, so urinalysis in isolated orchitis is usually normal.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Ascending spread through the vas deferens is the route of bacterial epididymitis, which typically produces pyuria.
whyWrongByChoice.B: The normal urinalysis reflects the route of infection, not viral suppression of leukocytes.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Mumps orchitis does not later progress to urethral infection; the urinary tract is not involved.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Parotitis does not explain the absence of pyuria; the urinary tract is simply not infected.

questions.stem: A 28-year-old man had mumps orchitis affecting both testes 2 years ago. He and his partner are planning a pregnancy and ask about his fertility. Approximately what proportion of adult men with this history have reduced fertility?

explanation.summary: Bilateral mumps orchitis reduces fertility in about 65% of affected adult men (unilateral about 25%).
explanation.whyCorrect: Untreated orchitis may reduce fertility, especially with mumps. Unilateral and bilateral mumps orchitis reduce fertility in about 25% and 65% of affected adult males, respectively; this man had bilateral disease.

whyWrongByChoice.A: 5% underestimates the impact; even unilateral mumps orchitis affects about 25%.
whyWrongByChoice.B: About 25% applies to unilateral mumps orchitis, not bilateral disease.
whyWrongByChoice.C: 45% does not match the reported figure of about 65% for bilateral disease.
whyWrongByChoice.E: 85% overstates the proportion; bilateral mumps orchitis reduces fertility in about 65%.

questions.stem: A 29-year-old HIV-negative man who has sex with men as the insertive partner during anal intercourse has 5 days of worsening left scrotal pain and fever. He has no urinary catheter or recent instrumentation. NAAT of first-void urine is negative for C. trachomatis and N. gonorrhoeae. Which of the following is the most likely causative organism?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Coxsackie B virus

choices.label: B
choices.text: Enterobacter species

choices.label: C
choices.text: Mumps orthorubulavirus

choices.label: D
choices.text: Mycobacterium tuberculosis

choices.label: E
choices.text: Treponema pallidum

explanation.summary: Insertive anal intercourse predisposes to coliform epididymitis (Citrobacter, Enterobacter), which is destructive and abscess-prone.
explanation.whyCorrect: Besides chlamydia and gonorrhea, an important cause of epididymitis in sexually active men, especially insertive partners in anal intercourse, is fecal coliform bacteria such as Citrobacter and Enterobacter. These organisms are highly destructive and tend to form abscesses.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Coxsackie B is a rare cause of viral orchitis, not coliform-exposure epididymitis.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Mumps causes orchitis by hematogenous spread in unvaccinated males, typically after parotitis.
whyWrongByChoice.D: M. tuberculosis is an uncommon cause of epididymitis seen especially in HIV-positive patients.
whyWrongByChoice.E: T. pallidum is a less common cause of epididymitis occurring as part of syphilis; his exposure favors fecal organisms.

questions.stem: A 24-year-old man comes to the clinic because of 3 days of burning on urination and a thick yellow-green discharge from the tip of his penis. Examination shows several small pustules on the penile shaft. A swab of the discharge is Gram stained. Which of the following findings is most likely?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Abundant neutrophils with no visible organisms

choices.label: B
choices.text: Gram-negative diplococci within neutrophils

choices.label: C
choices.text: Gram-negative rods scattered outside host cells

choices.label: D
choices.text: Gram-positive cocci in clusters within neutrophils

choices.label: E
choices.text: Gram-positive lancet-shaped diplococci outside cells

explanation.summary: Gonococcal urethritis produces purulent discharge whose Gram stain shows gram-negative diplococci inside phagocytes.
explanation.whyCorrect: Green, yellow, or white purulent urethral discharge with genital pustules and dysuria is the classic presentation of gonococcal urethritis. N. gonorrhoeae is a gram-negative, oxidase-positive diplococcus, and a Gram stain of a urethral swab shows the diplococci inside phagocytes, primarily neutrophils (occasionally some lie outside cells).

whyWrongByChoice.A: Neutrophils without visible organisms fit an organism that cannot be seen on Gram stain (e.g., C. trachomatis or M. genitalium), whose discharge is usually clear, not purulent.
whyWrongByChoice.C: N. gonorrhoeae is a diplococcus, not a rod, and it is classically seen inside neutrophils.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Gram-positive cocci in clusters describe staphylococci, not the cause of purulent urethritis with genital pustules.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Gram-positive lancet-shaped diplococci are not the pathogen of gonococcal urethritis, which stains gram-negative.

questions.stem: A 22-year-old woman has a cervical nucleic acid amplification test that is positive for Neisseria gonorrhoeae. Testing for other sexually transmitted infections was not performed. She is not pregnant and has no drug allergies. Which of the following is the most appropriate treatment?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Intramuscular ceftriaxone once plus a single dose of azithromycin

choices.label: B
choices.text: Intramuscular ceftriaxone once plus doxycycline for 7 days

choices.label: C
choices.text: Intramuscular gentamicin once plus a single dose of azithromycin

choices.label: D
choices.text: Oral cefixime alone as a single dose

choices.label: E
choices.text: Oral doxycycline alone for 7 days

explanation.summary: Uncomplicated gonorrhea is treated with a single IM dose of ceftriaxone, plus 7 days of doxycycline when chlamydia has not been excluded.
explanation.whyCorrect: Ceftriaxone given once intramuscularly is the recommended treatment for uncomplicated gonorrhea. Because coinfection with C. trachomatis is common and chlamydia has not been excluded here, doxycycline for 7 days is added. This approach reflects rising gonococcal resistance and avoids routine azithromycin in nonpregnant adults.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Azithromycin is no longer preferred for empiric dual therapy in nonpregnant adults; doxycycline is the chlamydial add-on.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Gentamicin plus azithromycin is reserved for patients with a severe cephalosporin allergy, which she does not have.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Cefixime is an alternative only when ceftriaxone is unavailable, and alone it provides no chlamydial coverage.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Doxycycline alone covers chlamydia but does not treat the confirmed gonococcal infection.

questions.stem: A 19-year-old man requests screening for sexually transmitted infections after a new partner. He has no symptoms. He would prefer to avoid a urethral swab. Which of the following is the best test to detect both gonorrhea and chlamydia?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Cell culture of a urethral specimen for inclusions

choices.label: B
choices.text: Culture of a urethral specimen on selective agar

choices.label: C
choices.text: Gram stain of discharge expressed from the urethra

choices.label: D
choices.text: Nucleic acid amplification testing of a urine sample

choices.label: E
choices.text: Serum antibody titers against both organisms

explanation.summary: NAAT is the standard diagnostic test for both gonorrhea and chlamydia and can be run on urine.
explanation.whyCorrect: Nucleic acid amplification testing has largely replaced culture for routine diagnosis. It is highly sensitive and specific, faster, and less invasive because it can be performed on urine rather than a swab, and it allows concurrent testing for other STIs such as trichomonas.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Because C. trachomatis is obligately intracellular, culture is rarely performed clinically and it requires an invasive specimen.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Culture on selective (Thayer-Martin) media is used mainly for gonococcal surveillance and susceptibility testing and does not grow chlamydia.
whyWrongByChoice.C: A Gram stain can suggest gonorrhea but cannot identify C. trachomatis, which is obligately intracellular.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Serology is not how either infection is diagnosed; molecular testing is the standard.

questions.stem: A microbiologist studying Chlamydia trachomatis isolates the small, dense form of the organism that is released when an infected epithelial cell ruptures. Which of the following best describes this form?

choices.label: A
choices.text: It divides by binary fission inside the host inclusion

choices.label: B
choices.text: It generates its own ATP to survive outside cells

choices.label: C
choices.text: It has a thick wall of classic peptidoglycan

choices.label: D
choices.text: It is the infectious form that enters new host cells

choices.label: E
choices.text: It persists in soil and animal hosts between infections

explanation.summary: The chlamydial elementary body is the small, dense, infectious form that enters host cells.
explanation.whyCorrect: Chlamydiae exist in two forms. The elementary body is small, dense, and infectious; it enters host cells and converts to a reticulate body, which replicates by fission inside a membrane-bound inclusion before reorganizing into elementary bodies that are released to infect neighboring cells.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Replication by binary fission inside the inclusion is the job of the reticulate body, not the released elementary body.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Chlamydiae cannot make their own ATP, which is part of why they are obligate intracellular pathogens.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Chlamydiae lack classic peptidoglycan because of reduced muramic acid.
whyWrongByChoice.E: C. trachomatis is an obligate human pathogen with no animal or environmental reservoir.

questions.stem: Several candidate vaccines against Neisseria gonorrhoeae have generated strong antibody responses in trial participants yet failed to prevent infection. Which of the following properties of the organism best explains this failure?

choices.label: A
choices.text: A thick antiphagocytic polysaccharide capsule

choices.label: B
choices.text: Absence of a peptidoglycan cell wall

choices.label: C
choices.text: Antigenic and phase variation of pili and LOS

choices.label: D
choices.text: Obligate intracellular growth within inclusions

choices.label: E
choices.text: Secretion of a protease that cleaves IgG

explanation.summary: Antigenic and phase variation of gonococcal surface molecules lets the organism evade antibodies, undermining vaccines and permitting reinfection.
explanation.whyCorrect: Antibodies to pili, LOS, and other surface molecules can block binding, but these molecules undergo antigenic variation (structural change) and phase variation (reversible on/off switching of expression). The many variants escape neutralizing antibodies, which explains the poor efficacy of candidate vaccines and repeated infections.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Gonococci do not produce a capsule, unlike N. meningitidis.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Lack of a peptidoglycan cell wall describes M. genitalium; gonococci are gram-negative with a cell wall.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Obligate intracellular growth in inclusions describes C. trachomatis, not N. gonorrhoeae.
whyWrongByChoice.E: The gonococcal protease cleaves IgA, not IgG, and it is not the reason vaccines fail.

questions.stem: A 23-year-old woman being treated for cervical gonorrhea with pelvic inflammatory disease develops sharp right upper quadrant pain that worsens with deep breaths and coughing. She also has nausea and a temperature of 38.6°C (101.5°F). Inflammation of which of the following structures most likely explains her new pain?

choices.label: A
choices.text: The collecting system of the right kidney

choices.label: B
choices.text: The epithelium of the common bile duct

choices.label: C
choices.text: The Glisson capsule of the liver

choices.label: D
choices.text: The pleura of the right lower lobe

choices.label: E
choices.text: The wall of the gallbladder

explanation.summary: Fitz-Hugh-Curtis syndrome is perihepatitis (Glisson capsule inflammation) complicating PID.
explanation.whyCorrect: Fitz-Hugh-Curtis syndrome is a complication of PID in which the Glisson capsule surrounding the liver becomes inflamed. It classically causes right upper quadrant pain worsened by breathing, coughing, or movement, with nausea, vomiting, and fever.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Renal inflammation is not linked to ascending gonococcal PID in this way.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Bile duct infection is not the upper-abdominal complication associated with PID.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Although the pain is pleuritic in quality, the process is perihepatic, not pleural.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Gallbladder inflammation is not the recognized complication of gonococcal PID; the capsule around the liver is.

questions.stem: A 21-year-old sexually active woman comes to the emergency department with fever and pain moving between several joints over 4 days. Examination shows tenderness and swelling along the tendon sheaths of the right wrist and a few scattered skin lesions on her forearms and legs. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Disseminated gonococcal infection

choices.label: B
choices.text: Fitz-Hugh-Curtis syndrome

choices.label: C
choices.text: Lymphogranuloma venereum

choices.label: D
choices.text: Reactive arthritis

choices.label: E
choices.text: Staphylococcal septic arthritis

explanation.summary: Disseminated gonococcal infection classically presents with the triad of polyarthritis, tenosynovitis, and dermatitis.
explanation.whyCorrect: Disseminated gonococcal infection presents with polyarthritis, tenosynovitis, and dermatitis. This young, sexually active woman has all three: pain in several joints, tendon sheath inflammation at the wrist, and skin lesions on the extremities.

whyWrongByChoice.B: Fitz-Hugh-Curtis syndrome causes pleuritic right upper quadrant pain, not arthritis and skin lesions.
whyWrongByChoice.C: LGV presents with proctocolitis, anal ulcers, and painful inguinal lymphadenopathy, not joint and skin findings.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Reactive arthritis after chlamydia is a sterile arthritis of the knees, ankles, or feet and does not produce the tenosynovitis-dermatitis triad.
whyWrongByChoice.E: S. aureus septic arthritis typically involves a single joint and lacks tenosynovitis with dermatitis.

questions.stem: A 6-week-old boy is brought to the physician because of a repetitive cough that comes in short, separate bursts, along with rapid breathing. His mother received no prenatal care, and he was delivered vaginally at home. Chest x-ray shows bilateral interstitial infiltrates, and a complete blood count shows eosinophilia. Which of the following organisms is the most likely cause?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Chlamydia trachomatis

choices.label: B
choices.text: Mycoplasma genitalium

choices.label: C
choices.text: Neisseria gonorrhoeae

choices.label: D
choices.text: Neisseria meningitidis

choices.label: E
choices.text: Staphylococcus aureus

explanation.summary: Neonatal C. trachomatis pneumonia causes staccato cough, tachypnea, bilateral interstitial infiltrates, and eosinophilia.
explanation.whyCorrect: Infants born vaginally to a parent with chlamydia can develop conjunctivitis or pneumonia. Chlamydial neonatal pneumonia is characterized by a staccato cough, tachypnea, bilateral interstitial infiltrates, and eosinophilia, exactly as in this infant.

whyWrongByChoice.B: M. genitalium is discussed as a cause of persistent urethritis, not neonatal pneumonia.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Neonatal gonococcal infection presents as purulent ophthalmia neonatorum; neonatal pneumonia is a chlamydial manifestation.
whyWrongByChoice.D: N. meningitidis is not associated with this vertically acquired pneumonia syndrome.
whyWrongByChoice.E: S. aureus does not produce this staccato-cough, interstitial, eosinophilic picture.

questions.stem: A 27-year-old woman at 14 weeks' gestation undergoes routine prenatal screening. Nucleic acid amplification testing is positive for Chlamydia trachomatis and negative for Neisseria gonorrhoeae. She has no drug allergies. Which of the following is the most appropriate treatment?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Intramuscular ceftriaxone

choices.label: B
choices.text: Intramuscular gentamicin

choices.label: C
choices.text: Oral azithromycin

choices.label: D
choices.text: Oral cefixime

choices.label: E
choices.text: Oral doxycycline

explanation.summary: When chlamydial coverage is needed in pregnancy, azithromycin is used because doxycycline is generally avoided.
explanation.whyCorrect: In nonpregnant adults doxycycline is the chlamydial agent, but it is generally avoided during pregnancy. The lecture specifies azithromycin for chlamydial coverage in pregnant patients.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Ceftriaxone is the gonococcal agent; her gonorrhea test is negative, and ceftriaxone does not treat chlamydia.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Gentamicin (with azithromycin) is an alternative gonorrhea regimen for severe cephalosporin allergy, not chlamydia therapy.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Cefixime is an alternative gonococcal agent when ceftriaxone is unavailable; it does not cover chlamydia.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Doxycycline is generally avoided in pregnancy and is used only if alternatives are unavailable.

questions.stem: A 4-day-old girl born in a hospital is brought to the clinic because of thick, purulent discharge from both eyes and marked eyelid swelling. Her parents declined all routine newborn medications after delivery. Gram stain of the discharge shows gram-negative diplococci within neutrophils. Which of the following is the most appropriate management?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Ceftriaxone, discharge home, and no evaluation of the mother

choices.label: B
choices.text: Ceftriaxone, evaluation for dissemination, and treating the mother

choices.label: C
choices.text: Erythromycin ointment, eye irrigation, and follow-up in one week

choices.label: D
choices.text: Oral azithromycin, chest radiograph, and reassurance of the mother

choices.label: E
choices.text: Topical erythromycin, lumbar puncture, and doxycycline for the mother

explanation.summary: Established gonococcal ophthalmia neonatorum requires ceftriaxone, evaluation for disseminated infection, and evaluation and treatment of the birthing parent.
explanation.whyCorrect: Purulent conjunctivitis 2-5 days after birth with gram-negative diplococci is gonococcal ophthalmia neonatorum. Once disease develops, erythromycin (a prophylactic agent) is no longer sufficient; standard treatment is ceftriaxone. The infant should be evaluated for disseminated infection, and the birthing parent should be evaluated and treated for gonorrhea.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Ceftriaxone is correct, but the infant must be assessed for dissemination and the birthing parent must be evaluated and treated.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Erythromycin ointment is prophylaxis given at birth; it is not sufficient treatment for established disease.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Azithromycin and a chest film fit a chlamydial picture; this is gonococcal disease, and the mother needs treatment, not reassurance.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Topical erythromycin is inadequate for established gonococcal disease, and doxycycline alone would not treat the mother's gonorrhea.

questions.stem: A 34-year-old man who has receptive anal intercourse comes to the physician because of 2 weeks of anal pain, fever, and a bloody, mucoid rectal discharge with a constant urge to defecate. Anoscopy shows several ulcers. One week later he develops painful, swollen inguinal lymph nodes. Which of the following is the most likely cause?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Chlamydia trachomatis serovars A, B, or C

choices.label: B
choices.text: Chlamydia trachomatis serovars D through K

choices.label: C
choices.text: Chlamydia trachomatis serovars L1, L2, or L3

choices.label: D
choices.text: Mycoplasma genitalium lacking a cell wall

choices.label: E
choices.text: Neisseria gonorrhoeae expressing variant pili

explanation.summary: Lymphogranuloma venereum (C. trachomatis L1-L3) presents in the US mainly as ulcerative proctocolitis that can progress to painful inguinal lymphadenopathy.
explanation.whyCorrect: LGV is a chronic infection caused by the more virulent, invasive C. trachomatis serovars L1, L2, and L3. Recent US cases have mostly presented as proctocolitis with anal ulcers, anal pain, mucoid or hemorrhagic rectal discharge, tenesmus, and fever, which may progress to painful inguinal lymphadenopathy.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Serovars A-C cause trachoma, an ocular infection spread by secretions, fomites, and flies.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Serovars D-K cause proctitis clinically similar to gonococcal proctitis, but ulcers with painful inguinal nodes point to the invasive L serovars.
whyWrongByChoice.D: M. genitalium is a cause of persistent urethritis, not ulcerative proctocolitis with lymphadenopathy.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Gonococcal proctitis causes itching, discharge, and tenesmus, but not ulcerative disease progressing to painful inguinal lymphadenopathy.

questions.stem: A 29-year-old woman is evaluated for infertility. Hysterosalpingography shows bilateral tubal scarring. She recalls a positive chlamydia screening test several years ago that was never treated, and she has never had pelvic pain or fever. Which of the following most directly caused the damage to her reproductive tract?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Cleavage of mucosal IgA by a bacterial protease

choices.label: B
choices.text: Direct lysis of epithelium by a secreted exotoxin

choices.label: C
choices.text: Endotoxin activity of bacterial lipooligosaccharide

choices.label: D
choices.text: Pilus-mediated resistance to neutrophil killing

choices.label: E
choices.text: Th1-driven chronic inflammation with IFN-γ release

explanation.summary: Chlamydial tissue damage is driven mainly by the host's Th1/IFN-γ immune response to persistent, often silent infection.
explanation.whyCorrect: Chlamydia-induced disease is driven largely by the host immune response. Persistent infection triggers chronic inflammation driven by Th1 cells and IFN-γ, and because infection is often asymptomatic, this immune-mediated damage can occur before diagnosis. Chlamydia causes PID more frequently and more silently than gonorrhea, hence its strong association with infertility and ectopic pregnancy.

whyWrongByChoice.A: IgA protease is a gonococcal virulence factor, not the mechanism of chlamydial scarring.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Injury from C. trachomatis is attributed to the immune response, not to a secreted exotoxin.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Lipooligosaccharide with endotoxin activity is a gonococcal virulence factor.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Pili that resist neutrophil killing belong to N. gonorrhoeae.

questions.stem: A 27-year-old man presents with 5 days of fever, sore throat, fatigue, and painful oral ulcers. Examination shows generalized lymphadenopathy and a faint maculopapular rash on his face, trunk, and extremities. Four weeks ago he had condomless receptive anal intercourse with a new partner. His CD4+ T cell count is 780/uL. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Acute retroviral syndrome of HIV infection

choices.label: B
choices.text: Clinically latent chronic HIV infection

choices.label: C
choices.text: Kaposi sarcoma in the setting of AIDS

choices.label: D
choices.text: Primary genital herpes simplex infection

choices.label: E
choices.text: Seborrheic dermatitis in the setting of AIDS

explanation.summary: Acute retroviral syndrome is a mononucleosis-like illness 3-6 weeks after HIV exposure with fever, pharyngitis, lymphadenopathy, maculopapular rash, and mucocutaneous ulcers.
explanation.whyCorrect: Many patients (40-90%) develop acute retroviral syndrome during the acute phase (0-12 weeks), most often 3-6 weeks after infection. Features include fever, lethargy, sore throat, generalized lymphadenopathy, a diffuse maculopapular rash of the face, trunk, and extremities, and mucocutaneous ulcerations. CD4+ counts may dip transiently but can remain in the normal range (500-1500/uL), as here.

whyWrongByChoice.B: The chronic phase is clinically latent and asymptomatic; this patient is acutely symptomatic weeks after exposure.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Kaposi sarcoma is a secondary neoplasm of AIDS; a CD4 count of 780/uL and a new febrile rash weeks after exposure do not fit.
whyWrongByChoice.D: HSV causes mucocutaneous ulcers but not a diffuse maculopapular rash with generalized lymphadenopathy and systemic illness after a high-risk exposure.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Seborrheic dermatitis produces red, flaky, greasy lesions in advanced disease, not an acute febrile maculopapular illness with a normal CD4 count.

questions.stem: A fourth-generation HIV screening immunoassay detects a viral capsid antigen, p24, in addition to host IgM and IgG against HIV-1/2. Which HIV gene encodes this antigen?

choices.label: A
choices.text: env

choices.label: B
choices.text: gag

choices.label: C
choices.text: pol

choices.label: D
choices.text: rev

choices.label: E
choices.text: tat

explanation.summary: gag encodes the structural proteins p24, p7, and p17 of the nucleocapsid and matrix.
explanation.whyCorrect: Three HIV genes encode proteins critical to its life cycle. gag encodes the structural proteins p24, p7, and p17 used in the nucleocapsid and matrix. p24 is the antigen detected by the HIV-1/2 antigen/antibody immunoassay.

whyWrongByChoice.A: env encodes the envelope glycoproteins gp120 and gp41 that mediate fusion.
whyWrongByChoice.C: pol encodes the enzymes reverse transcriptase, integrase, and protease, not structural capsid proteins.
